subject.title: fix(repair): publish only validated target commits

question: Should configurable repair runners permanently require the new Linux namespace and Landlock boundary and reject local or relative workspace dependency specifications?
rationale: This is an intentional trust-boundary choice that improves credential and publication safety but can disable previously usable runners and target layouts; tests cannot decide which compatibility contract the project wants to support.

options.title: Accept the strict boundary
options.body: Keep the fail-closed Linux/Landlock and dependency-source restrictions, require exact-head runtime proof, and document them as the supported repair-runner contract.

options.title: Preserve selected compatibility
options.body: Keep immutable exact-SHA publication but allow narrowly verified runner or workspace patterns with focused containment and upgrade tests.

options.title: Pause the broad rewrite
options.body: Do not merge until the patch can be reduced to a smaller publication-only boundary with separately reviewed execution containment.

recommendation.title: Accept the strict boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed Linux/Landlock and dependency-source restrictions, require exact-head runtime proof, and document them as the supported repair-runner contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history identifies this person as the sustained driver of the affected repair validation and publication design.
